title: DXF DICTIONARY late hard-owner flag after completed entries
status: bounded implementation with focused validation; no general graph qualification
problem: An ordinary DICTIONARY whose group 280 follows a complete entry is refused before typed or raw callbacks, preventing consumption of its otherwise intact object graph.

authority.scope: Group 280 is the dictionary-wide hard-owner flag; group 3 and 350 are per-entry names and soft-owner references.

fix: Within dxfRW::processDictionary, observe AcDbDictionary subclass scope. When group 280 occurs after complete entries in that scope, validate 0 or 1 and constant-time parser-local pending-entry completeness, retain the raw group, then update the typed flag. Other paths continue through the old parser. Entry codes 350/360 remain independently retained. Existing repeated-280 last-value behavior is retained, including when a later flag follows complete entries.
source_evidence: The ODA-returned AC1027 source contains DICTIONARY 0x78 owned by 0x70, hard-owner 1 and one 360 edge ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP→XRECORD 0x83 owned by 0x78. A controlled copy moves only that flag after the completed edge. Pre-fix selected-record read fails after root callback; fixed read publishes the dictionary with original flag, identity and edge. ODA 27.1 converts the full edited input to DWG and back to DXF; ezdxf verifies the dictionary and reciprocal XRECORD ownership and four XRECORD payload tags. The returned target was renumbered to 0x88. ODA invocation joins are manual; hashes alone do not prove lineage. The source is itself an ODA return from locally authored data; neither late order nor the edited copy is producer-authored.
tests: Fixture-free ASCII/Binary tests cover flag before/after and between completed entries, mixed 350/360 roles, independent raw source order, copy/assignment, rooted dictionary with two XRECORD outputs, reciprocal owners, typed readback, invalid values, pending name, unrelated subclass, 102 application-group scope, marker re-entry, unchanged WDFLT refusal and same-reader retry. A 1500-entry/1500-repeated-flag control covers the bounded-work path. The baseline test exits 2; the candidate passes. Target outputs are generated, not native application output. The lc3_compat_check target also builds. The unrelated existing libdxfrw_table_content_dxf_tests target fails to compile in the clean base snapshot: tests/object_physical_controls.h:25,29 repeats DRW_DxfObjectPhysicalSourcePolicy through dx_iface, triggering -Winaccessible-base under -Werror; those selectors were not run. After applying the separate test-only duplicate-base fix /private/tmp/object-physical-fix/object-physical.patch (SHA-256 e94d91246546989270b70027ac7fee13347ae5cdada1e5dc76ad0cd43b856cff), the candidate scratch build passes libdxfrw_objects_physical_sources, libdxfrw_dictionary_source_origins, and libdxfrw_dictionary_effective_ownership (3/3).
limitations: The selected physical record is checked through a minimal wrapper; no full physical file native output is claimed.
Newly allowed late repeated 280 uses existing last-value semantics, which is not a unique-source guarantee.
Direct protected parseCode, external subclasses and DICTIONARYWDFLT behavior are unchanged.
Flags inserted between an entry name and its handle remain refused.
Other unsupported or incomplete dictionary graphs, target remapping and external consumer/native behavior are not promoted.
ODA selected graph does not establish broader rendering or semantic compatibility.
